title: Web runtime disposal acknowledges an unfinished native browser-handoff helper
cause: Readiness started a detached handoff promise; no injected-context disposer owned its child. Error handling rejected before native close.
implementation: Connection-injection effect retains the handoff promise, aborts its helper on unload and joins native close. The helper records first failure, removes abort listeners on close and refuses pre-cancelled allocation. Intentional teardown suppresses manual browser-failure warnings.

verification.native: Shipped dsh --profile web boots with a private opener, creates an actual Node helper, unloads only web-runtime and observes helper exit before acknowledgement while the HTTP listener stays alive. Complete old bundle code observes a live helper after acknowledgement; explicit fixture cleanup then ends it. No desktop browser or model API is used.
verification.normalCases: The four original browser startup snapshots, including authentication, credential scrubbing, failure and SSH suppression, pass with the new owner snapshot on Node22 and Node24. Runtime repetitions are not extra unique cases.
verification.types: Changed unit and CLI snapshot faces have zero diagnostics; normal scoped package compile passes.
verification.build: Normal Web bundle emits index/startup and their shared public-url chunk; matching changed type-plane JS and declaration are captured.
verification.documentation: Twenty doc-quick gates, export JSDoc and complete catalog freshness checks pass.

rejectedCandidate.scope: Old URL publication after owner replacement before readiness
rejectedCandidate.conclusion: The pre-existing replacement regression already passes unchanged. No separate stale-URL bug is claimed.

allocationClassification: Administrative startup UI helper, not an agent/model workload. Its Node child is owned until close; the maintained opener keeps platform delegation and the post-handoff browser lifetime.
noteReview: Keep the active ready-Web-page note: application readiness, SSH URL ownership and OS delegation remain valid. New helper cleanup rationale complements it; no full supersession.
